# BOS Enterprise Capability Map - Gate 1

Estado: CERTIFIED / DOCUMENTAL CLOSURE
Fecha de materializacion: 2026-09-17
Fuente de evidencia certificada: `EDARSAHUB-ENTERPRISE-CAPABILITY-MAP-GATE1-R2-20260914`
Certificacion fuente: `CERTIFIED_READ_ONLY`
Quality gate fuente: `PASS`
Production touched en discovery: `false`
Files changed en discovery: `[]`

## 1. Objetivo

Este dossier materializa la interpretacion arquitectonica del Enterprise Capability Map de EDARSAHUB BOS a partir de la evidencia READ_ONLY ya certificada. No agrega discovery adicional ni declara capacidades por intuicion. Su funcion es fijar owners, patrones de reutilizacion y limites arquitectonicos para los Gates posteriores.

## 2. Principio rector

La secuencia obligatoria para cualquier nueva funcionalidad BOS es:

`REUSE -> CONSOLIDATE -> EXTRACT -> EXTEND -> CREATE_ONLY_WHEN_PROVEN_MISSING`

Crear una capacidad paralela queda prohibido cuando ya existe infraestructura canonica suficiente.

## 3. Matriz de capacidades

| Capability | Owner / implementacion observada | Estado | Decision vinculante |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity / Auth | `backend/modules/auth` | CANONICAL | REUSE |
| RBAC / Effective permissions | Auth + RBAC middleware + `menu-permissions` | CANONICAL | REUSE |
| Enterprise menus | SQL + protected frontend layout | EXISTS | CONSOLIDATE |
| Empresa / unidad / sucursal context | Auth context + resolvers | TRANSVERSAL | REUSE |
| Connection resolution | `core.connection_resolver`, server registry, SQL-first factories | CANONICAL_INFRA | EXTEND/SLIM |
| Scheduler | `core/scheduler/scheduler_manager.py` | CANONICAL_INFRA | REUSE |
| Jobs / resync / backfill | Scheduler + administrative APIs | EXISTS | CONSOLIDATE_ON_SCHEDULER |
| System / capability registry | `catalogos_sistemas.py` + capability resolver | EXISTS_PARTIAL | EXTEND_EXISTING |
| SoftRestaurant | Integration adapter/pattern | EXISTS | ADAPTER |
| MPRO | Integration adapter/pattern | EXISTS | ADAPTER |
| NetPay | Scheduler/resync integration | EXISTS | ADAPTER |
| vtiger | CRM external integration references | EXISTS_PARTIAL | EXTEND |
| Twilio | Notification provider | EXISTS | REUSE_PROVIDER |
| SAP / Oracle / Dynamics | Enterprise connector references | PARTIAL | ADAPTER_PATTERN |
| BBVA / Banorte | Banking integrations | PARTIAL | UNIVERSAL_BANKING_ADAPTERS |
| Dashboards / KPIs | Multiple consumers over backend services | EXISTS | CONSOLIDATE_METRIC_TRUTH |
| Workflows | Multiple domain implementations | EXISTS_FRAGMENTED | CONSOLIDATE_PRIMITIVES |
| Audit / evidence | APIs, tests, dossiers and Worker evidence | EXISTS | REUSE_COMMON_PATTERN |
| Agent runtime | Multiple `core.agent_*` capabilities | EXISTS_CORE_HEAVY | EXTRACT_PROGRESSIVELY |
| Universal Worker | `tools/mirror_sync` | CANONICAL_EXTERNAL_EXECUTION | KEEP_OUTSIDE_CORE |
| Repository READ_ONLY audit | `READ_ONLY` + `repository_contract_audit` | CANONICAL | REUSE |

## 4. Canonical owners

### 4.1 Identity and RBAC

Auth and RBAC are existing canonical capabilities. Domain modules must consume them and must not create independent permission engines, local role tables, hardcoded menu authorization or parallel user context.

### 4.2 Scheduler

`core.scheduler` is the scheduler kernel. Domains may contribute jobs but may not instantiate a second enterprise scheduler. Retry, scheduling, SLA and background orchestration should converge on this kernel where applicable.

### 4.3 Capability registry

The existing system catalog/capability resolver is the starting authority for capability registration. A second `CapabilityMaster`, `EnterpriseCapabilityRegistry` or equivalent parallel registry is forbidden without evidence that the existing registry cannot be extended.

### 4.4 Connection resolution

The shared connection resolver remains infrastructure, not a dumping ground for provider logic. Provider-specific behavior belongs behind adapters. The target dependency is `resolver -> system/provider type -> adapter`, not a growing chain of provider conditionals in Core.

## 5. Existing capabilities

Gate 1 confirms high reusable infrastructure. The project is not greenfield. The principal existing enterprise primitives include identity, RBAC, context, scheduler, SQL-first connection factories, system/capability catalog, resync/backfill patterns, integrations, audit/evidence patterns, dashboards/KPIs and agent infrastructure.

`TRUE_GREENFIELD_NEED=LOW`

## 6. Duplication risks

### HIGH
- Parallel RBAC or permission systems inside domains.
- Parallel schedulers.
- New system/capability registries instead of extending the existing one.
- Provider-specific connection stacks for BBVA, Banorte, NetPay, MPRO, SoftRestaurant, SAP, Oracle or Dynamics.

### MEDIUM-HIGH
- Repeated workflow state/SLA/authorization logic by domain.
- Repeated health/retry/audit behavior by integration.
- Multiple KPI definitions for the same business metric.
- Agent capabilities continuing to accumulate directly under Core.

## 7. Orphan / ambiguous ownership candidates

The following classes of artifacts require owner clarification rather than immediate new development:

- Legacy catalog helpers such as SoftRestaurant consultation artifacts outside a clear bounded context.
- Historical audit JSON/dossier artifacts stored near runtime code.
- Provider-specific utilities whose responsibility overlaps connection resolution, catalog or scheduler.

Rule: classify first as runtime source, test evidence, audit artifact or documentation before any migration/deletion.

## 8. Missing or incomplete enterprise capabilities

These are gaps of formalization, not evidence for greenfield subsystems.

### 8.1 Capability Registry completeness
Extend the existing registry to represent, when justified by later Gates: owner, domain, APIs, SQL objects, permissions, jobs, integrations, status, version and dependencies.

### 8.2 Workflow primitives
Formalize common primitives for state, transition, authorization, SLA, escalation, evidence and notification where repeated implementations are proven. Avoid a monolithic engine unless evidence requires it.

### 8.3 Universal integration contract
Converge adapters on common contracts such as connect, health, sync, backfill, retry, audit, credentials, rate limit and status. Do not create one infrastructure stack per provider.

### 8.4 Data provenance / freshness
Standardize source, source_type, as_of, freshness/stale state, sync job and last_success metadata for synchronized administrative/reporting data.

### 8.5 Capability dependency graph
Represent dependencies by extending the capability registry when a later Gate proves the required persistence and graph semantics.

## 9. Core overgrowth

`CORE_OVERGROWTH=CONFIRMED`
`SEVERITY=MEDIUM_HIGH`

Core should retain only stable enterprise primitives: security, identity/context primitives, DB/SQL primitives, RBAC primitives, configuration, connection abstractions and scheduler kernel.

Progressive extraction candidates include agent runtime policies, external research, provider-specific orchestration and domain-specific behavior. This dossier does not authorize moving code; each extraction requires its own bounded Gate and regression evidence.

## 10. Target architecture

```text
EDARSAHUB BOS
|
+-- CORE SLIM
|   +-- Identity / Security primitives
|   +-- RBAC primitives
|   +-- SQL / DB primitives
|   +-- Context
|   +-- Connection abstractions
|   +-- Scheduler kernel
|
+-- ENTERPRISE SERVICES
|   +-- Capability Registry
|   +-- Workflow primitives
|   +-- Integration Runtime
|   +-- Audit / Provenance
|   +-- Notifications
|   +-- Agent Runtime
|
+-- DOMAIN MODULES
|   +-- Comercial
|   +-- Finanzas
|   +-- Compras
|   +-- Operaciones / Inventarios
|   +-- RH
|   +-- CRM
|   +-- Proveedores
|   +-- Cavas
|   +-- Hospitality
|
+-- ADAPTERS
|   +-- SoftRestaurant
|   +-- MPRO
|   +-- NetPay
|   +-- vtiger
|   +-- Twilio
|   +-- BBVA
|   +-- Banorte
|   +-- SAP
|   +-- Oracle
|   +-- Dynamics
|
+-- EXTERNAL EXECUTION INFRA
    +-- Universal Worker
```

## 11. Binding rules for subsequent Gates

1. EDARSAHUB SQL Server remains the canonical operational brain.
2. MongoDB may not be introduced as operational truth or fallback.
3. Administrative dashboards may not depend directly on LIVE sources.
4. Reuse canonical Auth/RBAC; no domain RBAC forks.
5. Reuse canonical Scheduler; no parallel schedulers.
6. Extend the existing capability registry before creating a new registry or catalog.
7. Integration providers must be adapters of shared infrastructure, not independent subsystems.
8. BBVA and Banorte are adapters of a Universal Banking Connector, not independent banking architectures.
9. KPI consumers must share canonical metric definitions and sources.
10. Domain workflows must reuse common primitives when repetition is proven.
11. New files under `backend/core` require explicit evidence that the capability is truly transversal and cannot live in an enterprise service/module.
12. Universal Worker remains outside application Core.
13. No future Gate may infer a missing capability only because a preferred class/file name is absent; absence must be proven functionally.
14. Any CREATE decision must document why REUSE, CONSOLIDATE, EXTRACT and EXTEND were insufficient.
15. Production changes require explicit authorization and are outside this Gate.
